objects.taxonomy_description: Stocky tailless marsupial measuring 60-85 cm in body length with robust rounded body form. Fur is dense, woolly, and grey-brown with distinctive white patches on chest, ears, and rump. Ears are large, rounded, and prominently furry with white marginal tufts. Nose is broad, leathery, and black with distinctive textured surface. Limbs are powerful with five digits each; forefeet feature two opposable thumbs for gripping eucalyptus branches. Claws are sharp and curved for climbing. Body exhibits stocky proportions with broad chest and rounded abdomen. Head is broad with small eyes and inconspicuous ears relative to body size. Weight ranges 4-15 kg with sexual dimorphism. Posture is typically upright when seated on branches.

objects.taxonomy_description: Small Old World monkey measuring 30-60 cm body length weighing 2-8 kg. Body covered with long hair around face forming distinctive facial ruff. Fur coloration variable by species in gray, brown, olive, or red. Face bare with expressive features. Eyes forward-facing with brown irises. Nose narrow. Ears small. Tail long and non-prehensile. Hind limbs elongated. Body slender and agile. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. African arboreal monkey with complex social behavior.

objects.taxonomy_description: Edible fungus with a characteristic cap-and-stem morphology. The cap (pileus) is convex to flat, typically 3-10 cm in diameter, with a smooth or slightly scaly surface in white, brown, or tan coloration. The underside reveals gills (lamellae) radiating from the stem, ranging from white to dark brown. The cylindrical stem (stipe) is smooth, firm, and white, typically 3-8 cm in length. The overall form is umbrella-like with a fleshy, moist texture.
